name: Arms akimbo stance

card.summary: The arms akimbo stance, hands on hips with elbows out, is a posture that widens the upper-body silhouette and is read by many as assertive.
card.note: Gym forum users also describe it as a stereotype of bodybuilders.

quick.overview:
Arms akimbo means standing with hands on the hips and elbows pointing outward. It makes the torso look wider and takes up more space, which is the quality researchers call postural expansion.

The appearance payoff people point to is a broader, more confident presence. Research on expansive postures links them with signals of dominance and pride; studies specifically of this stance for looks are limited.
quick.how: People adopt it while standing in photos, presentations or the gym. Researchers also use the stance in exercise studies, where jumpers keep hands on hips to standardise movement.
quick.risks: No physical risks are reported. Some gym forum posters describe it as a stereotypical bodybuilder habit and as looking oafy, and one user recalls being told to stop standing that way.

lead: The arms akimbo stance, standing with hands on the hips and elbows out, widens the visible outline of the upper body and is commonly read as assertive or confident.

Psychology research on postural expansion, how much space the body takes up, has linked expansive postures with expressing dominance and pride, and a 2023 study in Emotion examined specific forms of expansiveness and their interaction with other postural elements such as arm position.[1] Separately, sports scientists use hands-on-hips as a standard control: studies of jump performance have participants jump with arms akimbo.[2][3]

On T Nation, members describe the stance as a bodybuilder stereotype, with one post saying good posture lets the arms hang in front of the lats instead.[4] No studies have tested the stance as a looks intervention.

chain: Wider torso outline, more space taken
Reads as broader and more assertive
angle.text: The pose enlarges the upper-body silhouette and is associated with expansive, dominant body language. People use it in photos and social settings to look broader and more confident.

paras: The posture places the hands on the hips with elbows pointed outward. In research on postural expression, expansiveness refers to how much space the body takes up, and arm position is one of the elements examined alongside it.[1]

Because it standardises arm movement, hands-on-hips is used in counter-movement jump tests; one study tested 1,835 children and adolescents jumping on a force platform with arms akimbo.[2] A 2024 biomechanics study compared akimbo and bent-in-front arm positions on jump metrics.[3]

On T Nation the stance is mentioned as a hallmark of a stereotypical bodybuilder,[4] and another poster describes people standing arms akimbo in the weight room as needing to control their bodies better.[5]
No studies found on the stance as an appearance technique. Related research on expansive posture and dominance signalling exists.[1]

lore.intro: Forum mentions are incidental and mostly describe the stance as a gym stereotype.[4]

claims.claim: Standing arms akimbo makes you look bigger and more dominant
claims.believers: Gym users note it is associated with bodybuilders, who tend to stand this way to appear broad.[4]
claims.experts: A 2023 study found postural expansion expresses dominance and high-arousal positive affect, with arm position interacting with other elements.[1]
